title: What Happens When Your Muscles Get Sore Days Later?
description:
Send this to the friend who walks down stairs sideways after leg day.
Muscle soreness after a workout usually sets in one to three days later. It isn't lactic acid (that's mostly gone within about an hour, Houston Methodist); it comes from tiny tears in your muscle fibers, and the ache builds over hours. Moves where a muscle works while it lengthens, like lowering a weight, lunges or running downhill, are the likeliest to cause it (Cleveland Clinic). Cleveland Clinic says see a provider if the pain lasts more than a week or feels sharp and constant, and get urgent help if your pee is unusually dark or bloody.

safety: Curious-friend tone, no personal medical advice; the only guidance is Cleveland Clinic's 'see a provider if pain lasts more than a week' and 'unusually dark or bloody pee' (emergency room for rhabdomyolysis symptoms), voiced as 'Dark pee, or sore past a week? Get help fast.' No supplement or painkiller tips voiced. Lactic acid is presented as cleared only because Houston Methodist (physical therapist Corbin Hedt) sources both 'isn't from lactic acid buildup at all' and 'gone within about an hour'. No gore: tears are schematic nicks in rope-like fibers.
